blogs.title: The Silent Desaturator: When Hypoxia Lacks Symptoms
blogs.description: This post examines the paradoxical phenomenon of severe oxygen desaturation without respiratory distress ('air hunger'). It explores the central mechanism of brainstem compression disrupting afferent signals, distinguishing this 'silent' central hypoventilation from obstructive sleep apnea and other causes of hypoxia.

blogs.title: Dysphagia Without Dyspepsia: Neurogenic Choking When GI Workup Is Normal
blogs.description: A guide to the diagnostic algorithm for unexplained choking. It emphasizes that normal laryngoscopy and endoscopy in patients with bulbar symptoms warrants a neurological workup, highlighting the prevalence of Chiari Malformation Type I in patients with persistent dysphagia after GI exclusion.

blogs.title: The Power of Stewardship: Uncovering Chiari Through Historical CT Review
blogs.description: This post discusses the clinical utility of re-evaluating archived imaging when a patient presents with vague chronic symptoms. It provides specific radiographic signs of a crowded foramen magnum on CT scans and emphasizes the importance of longitudinal imaging review in undiagnosed case workups.

blogs.title: Scalp Allodynia and Vertex Pain: A Neurological Clue Missed for Decades
blogs.description: Focuses on the diverse headache phenomenology of Chiari Malformation, specifically moving beyond classic occipital pain to discuss vertex allodynia and cutaneous sensitivity. It highlights the link between scalp pain and cerebellar tonsillar compression, suggesting hair trimming as a diagnostic clue.

blogs.title: Acquired or Unmasked? Separating Trauma Sequelae from Primary Chiari Malformation
blogs.description: Analyzes the temporal relationship between head trauma and symptom onset in CMI. The post explores the ambiguity between traumatic tonsillar herniation versus unmasking a pre-existing malformation, offering guidance on interpreting history in the context of a 'new' diagnosis found on historical imaging.

blogs.title: Disability vs. Decompression: Navigating the Decision Curve in Adult Chiari Type I
blogs.description: An overview of clinical decision-making regarding surgical intervention in symptomatic adults. It discusses the tension between conservative monitoring and operative decompression, focusing on the criteria for intervention (progression of symptoms vs. severity of imaging findings) and the patient's quality of life.
